headline: Cash App now lets you stop subscription charges on your Cash App Card, and its new bills tool may ask for your passwords
tldr: Cash App's terms dropped "No Right to Stop Payment": you can now block recurring card charges 3 business days ahead. A new Bills and Subscriptions tool can act for you with power of attorney.
who: Cash App Card holders with subscriptions or automatic payments on the card, and anyone who turns on Cash App's new Bills and Subscriptions feature
seo_title: Cash App terms Nov 2026: stop payment on subscriptions, new Bills and Subscriptions
seo_desc: Cash App's Nov 25, 2026 terms replace 'No Right to Stop Payment' with a right to stop preauthorized Cash App Card charges 3 business days ahead, and add a Bills and Subscriptions service with power of attorney.

redline.before: 6. No Right to Stop Payment You do not have the right to stop payment on a transaction originated with your Cash App Card.
redline.after: 6. Right to Stop Payment You have the right to stop payment on preauthorized transfers originated with your Cash App Card.
redline.label: Terms of Service · Cash App Card, section 6
redline.note: Recurring charges on the card can now be stopped, if Cash App hears from you three business days before the charge.

redline.after: You grant us and the Bills and Subscriptions Vendor a limited power of attorney and appoint us and the Bills and Subscriptions Vendor as your lawful attorneys-in-fact and agents, each with the authority to act independently or jointly, to access your Linked Subscriptions
redline.label: Terms of Service · XXV. Bills and Subscriptions
redline.note: The new bills tool works by logging in to your merchant accounts on your behalf.

redline.after: Blocking a merchant does not automatically cancel underlying subscriptions or agreements with the merchant.
redline.label: Terms of Service · Right to Stop Payment
redline.note: Stopping the payment isn't the same as cancelling: you may still owe the merchant.

actions: To stop a recurring Cash App Card charge, open Cash App, go to the Activity tab and block the merchant at least 3 business days before the charge date (or write via Cash App Support, or call (800) 969-1940)
Cancel the subscription with the merchant too: blocking "does not automatically cancel underlying subscriptions or agreements with the merchant"
Before turning on Bills and Subscriptions, know that it may ask for your merchant usernames and passwords, which go to an outside vendor under that vendor's own terms
what:
Cash App's [Terms of Service](https://cash.app/legal/us/en-us/tos), now marked "Last Updated: November 25, 2026", change two things for people who pay subscriptions with a Cash App Card (fetched November 26, 2026).

## Change 1: you can now stop recurring card charges

The card section used to say "6. No Right to Stop Payment" and "You do not have the right to stop payment on a transaction originated with your Cash App Card." It now reads "6. Right to Stop Payment": "You have the right to stop payment on preauthorized transfers originated with your Cash App Card. To stop payment on a preauthorized transfer, we must receive your request at least three (3) Business Days before the scheduled date of the transfer." Preauthorized transfers are defined as "automatic payments, subscriptions, or recurring payments" where a merchant stores your card.

The way to do it is to block the merchant: "Open Cash App, go to the Activity tab, and block the merchant", write through Cash App Support in the app, or call (800) 969-1940. "If you call, we may also require you to put your request in writing and if you fail to do so within 14 days, the stop payment may be removed." Two catches: "blocking a merchant will result in blocking all future Cash App Card transactions from that merchant", and "Blocking a merchant does not automatically cancel underlying subscriptions or agreements with the merchant." If Cash App misses a request made three business days or more ahead, "we will be liable for your unrecoverable losses."

How it compares (checked Nov 26): the wording mirrors the federal Regulation E stop-payment rule, which says a consumer "may stop payment of a preauthorized electronic fund transfer from the consumer's account by notifying the financial institution orally or in writing at least three business days before the scheduled date of the transfer" and lets the institution ask for written confirmation "within 14 days of an oral notification" (12 CFR 1005.10(c)).

## Change 2: a new Bills and Subscriptions service

A new section XXV describes "an optional service that allows you to view and manage recurring third-party merchant bills and subscriptions connected to your Cash App Card", run directly or through an outside "Bills and Subscriptions Vendor". Turning it on authorizes Cash App and the vendor to do things including "adding, updating, or blocking your Cash App Card for payment of Linked Subscriptions" and "viewing transactions, managing, making changes, and canceling Linked Subscriptions."

To do that, "you may be required to create an account with the Bills and Subscriptions Vendor and supply the Bills and Subscriptions Vendor with your credentials including, but not limited to, usernames, passwords, PIN numbers", and you grant both "a limited power of attorney". Cash App "may use the data from your Linked Subscriptions" for the service "and for any other purposes disclosed in the" Cash App Privacy Notice. Pricing, cancellation and refund terms of each subscription "are strictly between you and the third-party merchant", supported subscriptions can be removed "at any time and for any reason" without notice, and if a connection is lost "it is solely your responsibility to update such connections". "We do not charge a fee for your use of the Bills and Subscriptions Service."

Other changes: "Cash App Credit Score" is renamed "Cash App Score" in the contents; the card section adds wording for Sponsored Accounts for a Child ("you authorize the Child to conduct transactions with the Cash App Card"); two sentences were removed from the card section ("We make no guarantees regarding your Cash App Card and we are not responsible if it gets stolen, lost, destroyed, or used without your permission, except as otherwise described in these Cash App Terms." and an older duplicate negative-balance line), while the remaining sentence still says the Company "is not responsible if your Cash App Card is lost, stolen, destroyed, or used without your permission" except as the terms or law say otherwise.
faq: Can I stop a subscription payment on my Cash App Card?

Yes, as of the November 25, 2026 terms: "You have the right to stop payment on preauthorized transfers originated with your Cash App Card." Cash App must get the request at least three business days before the charge; you do it by blocking the merchant in the Activity tab, via Cash App Support, or by calling (800) 969-1940.
Does blocking a merchant in Cash App cancel my subscription?
No. Cash App's terms say "Blocking a merchant does not automatically cancel underlying subscriptions or agreements with the merchant." Cancel with the merchant as well.
What is Cash App Bills and Subscriptions?

An optional service to "view and manage recurring third-party merchant bills and subscriptions connected to your Cash App Card". It may require giving an outside vendor your merchant usernames and passwords and granting Cash App and the vendor a limited power of attorney. Cash App says it doesn't charge a fee for it.
sources: Cash App Terms of Service, Last Updated November 25, 2026 (fetched Nov 26, 2026)
12 CFR 1005.10(c), Consumer's right to stop payment (eCFR)

headline: YouTube TV's free trial is now 2 days on every plan, down from 5 (and 10 a week ago)
tldr: YouTube TV's plans page now shows a "2-day free trial" on every plan, down from 5 days yesterday and 10 days on Nov 20. Your first charge comes days sooner.
who: People thinking of trying YouTube TV, including its main plan and genre plans; current members aren't affected
seo_title: YouTube TV free trial now 2 days (was 5, and 10 on Nov 20)
seo_desc: YouTube TV's explore-plans page now shows a 2-day free trial on every plan (Nov 26, 2026), down from 5 days on Nov 25 and 10 days on Nov 20. Prices and Dec 2 offers unchanged.

redline.label: Explore plans · YouTube TV main plan
redline.note: The same 5-to-2 cut appears on every plan card on the page.

redline.label: Explore plans · most plans, Nov 20 vs Nov 26
redline.note: Our Nov 20 capture showed 10 days on most plans; Nov 22 to 25 showed 5.

actions: If you start a trial, set a reminder for the next day: the trial is now 2 days, after which the plan's price is charged
If you only want YouTube TV for one event, compare the 2-day trial with the new-user promo prices on the same page, which end December 2, 2026
what:
YouTube TV's [explore-plans page](https://tv.youtube.com/learn/explore-plans/) now shows "2-day free trial" on every plan card (fetched November 26, 2026). On November 22 to 25 the same cards said "5-day free trial", except the Sports plan, which already showed "2-day free trial". When we captured the page for our [YouTube TV plans and prices guide](https://quietlychanged.com/guides/youtube-tv-plans-and-prices-2026-every-price-increase/) on November 20, most plans showed a "10-day free trial". So in under a week the trial on most plans went from 10 days to 2.

What stays the same: prices and the limited-time offers for new users are unchanged. The main plan still lists $82.99/mo, with the promo at $59.99/mo, and Sports + News $71.99/mo with a $49.99/mo promo ("Save $132 total on your first 6 months"). The fine print still says "After promotional period, you will be charged the then current rate per month" and "Offer ends December 2, 2026." YouTube TV doesn't say on the page why the trial changed or whether it's temporary.
faq: How long is the YouTube TV free trial?
As of November 26, 2026, YouTube TV's plans page shows a "2-day free trial" on every plan. It showed 5 days on November 22 to 25 and 10 days on most plans on November 20.
No. The plans page still lists the main plan at $82.99/mo and the new-user offers that end December 2, 2026.
sources: YouTube TV explore plans page (fetched Nov 26, 2026)
QuietlyChanged: YouTube TV plans and prices 2026 (Nov 20 capture)
